qt: to the Commission Lars Patrick Berg (ECR) Subject:
Regulation (EU) 2022/10321 required the Member States to provide ‘financial incentives or compensation to market participants’ involved in meeting the EU’s ‘filling targets’. Can the Commission: 1.

indicate which Member States are yet to enact appropriate measures applying to all market participants, both private and state-owned, that played a role in helping the EU to meet its gas storage targets, and
indicate what action has been taken to date against Member States that have failed to adopt and implement measures that fully meet the requirements set out in Regulation (EU) 2022/1032?

Regulation (EU) 2022/1032 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 June 2022 amending Regulations (EU) 2017/1938 and (EC) No 715/2009 with regard to gas storage (OJ L 173, 30.6.2022, p. 17).
at: (English version) to the Commission Lars Patrick Berg (ECR) (24 January 2024) Subject: Gas storage Regulation (EU) 2022/1032 (1) required the Member States to provide ‘financial incentives or compensation to market participants’ involved in meeting the EU’s ‘filling targets’. Can the Commission: 1.

indicate which Member States are yet to enact appropriate measures applying to all market participants, both private and state-owned, that played a role in helping the EU to meet its gas storage targets, and
indicate what action has been taken to date against Member States that have failed to adopt and implement measures that fully meet the requirements set out in Regulation (EU) 2022/1032?

(12 March 2024) The regulation (EU) 2022/1032 (2) provides that Member States must take all necessary measures to meet the filling targets. They should aim to use market-based measures where possible to avoid unnecessary market disruption. Measures may include regulatory measures, financial incentives, or compensation to market participants. The regulation provides an illustrative and non-exhaustive list of potential measures and tools. Some of the measures existed prior to the gas storage regulation of 2022, while others were established after its adoption. Most common measures implemented by Member States were, for instance, imposing an obligation on Storage Operators on the minimum filling level to achieve, in line with the national objective or by requiring tendering the capacities to market participants; or by adopting effective instruments for the purchase and management of strategic stocks by public or private entities. So far, there is no Member State which fails to adopt and implement measures to meet the requirements set out in Regulation (EU) 2022/1032. According to Article 17a of Regulation (EU) 2017/1938, inserted by Article 1(5) of the Storage Regulation, the Commission adopted the annual report on the main aspects on gas storages implementation to the European Parliament and the Council and published it on 27 February 2024.

Regulation (EU) 2022/1032 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 June 2022 amending Regulations (EU) 2017/1938 and (EC) No 715/2009 with regard to gas storage (OJ L 173, 30.6.2022, p. 17).
